title: Sections vanishing on other components extend from one component
statement: Let $Y$ be a reduced scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-reduced-scheme] whose underlying space is the union of finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$, each given its reduced closed subscheme structure [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $Z\subset Y$ be the reduced closed subscheme supported on $Z_2\cup\cdots\cup Z_r$, let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ be its ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $\mathcal I_1$ be the image of $\mathcal I|_{Z_1}$ in $\mathcal O_{Z_1}$. For any invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal M$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and any $m\ge0$, restriction is an isomorphism $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal I\mathcal M^{\otimes m})\cong\Gamma(Z_1,\mathcal I_1(\mathcal M|_{Z_1})^{\otimes m})$. A section on the right therefore extends uniquely as a section of $\mathcal M^{\otimes m}$ on $Y$ which vanishes on $Z$; its nonvanishing locus (as in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]) lies in $Z_1$ and agrees there with that of the original section.

source.place: Varieties Remark 09NW (varieties-remark-conductor), applied to the component cover, and Lemma 09NX proof, conductor equality of global sections

proof.text: Use [lem-sc-conductor-sections-restriction] to obtain an additive bijection of ideal tensor sections compatible with the canonical restriction map. Form its additive equivalence using AddEquiv.ofBijective. Tensoring the target ideal inclusion by the invertible pulled-back tensor power is a monomorphism, hence is injective on global sections.

For a section s on the distinguished component, take its inverse image q under the equivalence and define t to be its image under ideal multiplication. Compatibility proves its required restriction. The kernel characterisation [lem-sc-closed-immersion-ideal-tensor-sections] proves that t vanishes on Z. For any competing t, that characterisation supplies q prime in the ideal tensor sections. Injectivity of the target ideal inclusion implies r(q prime)=s=r(q), and injectivity of r then gives q prime=q and equality of the ambient sections.

A section vanishing on Z cannot be nonvanishing at any point of its image, by [lem-sc-nonvanishing-tensor-pullback] and the zero-germ criterion. The component cover and the description of the image of Z therefore put every nonvanishing point in the distinguished component. Apply the same pullback criterion to that component, using the prescribed restricted section, to prove equality of loci in both directions.

lean.statement: theorem conductor_sections {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced Y] {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (C : ι → Scheme.{u}) (i : ∀ b : ι, C b ⟶ Y) [∀ b : ι, IsReduced (C b)] [∀ b : ι, IsClosedImmersion (i b)] (hcomponents : ∀ b : ι, Set.range (i b) ∈ irreducibleComponents Y) (hdistinct : Function.Injective fun b : ι => Set.range (i b)) (hcover : (⋃ b : ι, Set.range (i b)) = Set.univ) (a : ι) {Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced Z] (j : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion j] (hZ : Set.range j = ⋃ b : ι, ⋃ (_ : b ≠ a), Set.range (i b)) (M : Y.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] (m : ℕ) : let N := M.tensorPow m let N₁ := (tensorPullback (i a)).obj N let adj₁ := Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction (i a)) let adjZ := Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction j) let res₁ : Γ(N, ⊤) → Γ(N₁, ⊤) := fun t ↦ (adj₁.unit.app N).val.app (op ⊤) t let resZ : Γ(N, ⊤) → Γ((tensorPullback j).obj N, ⊤) := fun t ↦ (adjZ.unit.app N).val.app (op ⊤) t let I := j.ker let I₁ := I.comap (i a) let μ : I.toModules ⊗ N ⟶ N := I.toModulesι ▷ N ≫ (λ_ N).hom let μ₁ : I₁.toModules ⊗ N₁ ⟶ N₁ := I₁.toModulesι ▷ N₁ ≫ (λ_ N₁).hom ∃ e : Γ(I.toModules ⊗ N, ⊤) ≃+ Γ(I₁.toModules ⊗ N₁, ⊤), (∀ s, μ₁.app ⊤ (e s) = res₁ (μ.app ⊤ s)) ∧ ∀ s : Γ(I₁.toModules ⊗ N₁, ⊤), (∃! t : Γ(N, ⊤), res₁ t = μ₁.app ⊤ s ∧ resZ t = 0) ∧ ∀ t : Γ(N, ⊤), res₁ t = μ₁.app ⊤ s → resZ t = 0 → nonvanishingLocus N t = i a '' nonvanishingLocus N₁ (μ₁.app ⊤ s)
